scenes.headline: How MrFlow climbs resolution without diffusion steps
scenes.sub: A training-free reshuffle: low-res steps, an upscaler, one refine step.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Dumpling! Image models run every denoising step at full resolution. MrFlow moves most of that work somewhere cheaper, with no retraining. Here's how.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Take the steps small, upscale in pixel space, then refine once at full size.
scenes.say: Structure settles early and is cheap to compute small. So spend the diffusion steps at low resolution, climb with an upscaler, and refine once at full size.

steps.say: First, run twelve of the usual twenty steps at low resolution. They're cheap there, and that's where the layout gets fixed.
Decode, and upscale the picture in pixel space with an off-the-shelf super-resolution network. One forward pass, not more diffusion.
Encode it back, and add a small amount of noise, computed from the schedule. No extra network, no training.
Then a single full-resolution step pulls the detail back into the model's own distribution, and cleans up the upscaler's artifacts.

left.title: Latent upsampling
left.say: The usual trick also starts small, but climbs by running more diffusion steps at the higher resolution.

right.title: MrFlow
items: One diffusion step to clean up
right.say: MrFlow climbs with a cheap upscaler instead, and buys back fidelity with one step.

scenes.label: faster, training-free, at near-native quality on the good configs
scenes.note: best case: FLUX pushed to (12, 1) loses about 18% on OneIG
scenes.say: On the good settings, that's four to nine times faster at near-native quality. Push it harder, or pick a brittle model, and quality drops.

scenes.text: Structure is cheap and settles early. Resolution can be borrowed from an upscaler, and cleaned up in one step.

recap: Upscale in pixels, add a little noise
scenes.say: To recap: plan small, upscale in pixels, and refine once.
